agent.problem: Story cards 3, 5, 7, 8 and 12 each exceed two sentences. Card 5, for example, runs to six short sentences, and card 12 has four.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: Saying that the 25-cent sticker was on Papa Dorin's face adds a new detail to his backstory. The provided story says that he was in a bin at the closing bakery and had a 25-cent price sticker, but does not place that sticker on his face.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

agent.problem: The card explicitly uses the dancing and tambourines from verse 3 as well as the reason introduced in verse 4, but it cites only Psalm 149:4. Its citation needs to begin with the first verse it uses.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

agent.problem: Too many choices depend on guessing an unrevealed detail. Cards 2, 4 and 6 are detail-discovery questions, while cards 11, 15 and 16 also lack enough context for a reasoned answer. Consequently, most of the stop's choices are not informed guesses, and the discoveries amount to more than a few.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: The setup says only that the LORD adorns or dresses up the afflicted. Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason out "salvation"; the baker must guess the unseen wording from three possibilities.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: Saying only that the psalm "turns serious" gives no reasoned path from praises in the saints' mouths to a sword in their hands. Choosing sword rather than scroll or torch is therefore a guess at an unseen detail.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
